subject: literature
intro: Literature leads to paid work with words at professional standard — writing fiction and copy, shaping other people's manuscripts, reporting the news, documenting technology, and teaching texts in universities.

roles.title: Writers and Authors
roles.what: Originate and prepare written material such as scripts, stories and advertisements — developing plots, characters and voice into finished work for print, stage, screen or online publication.
roles.where: The prose unit's work on plot, narrative shape and tension, and the poetry unit's attention to form and language, are the crafts of shaping a story this role practises; close reading trains the sentence-level control their drafts need.

roles.title: Editors
roles.what: Plan, coordinate and revise written material for publication — reviewing proposals and drafts, restructuring weak passages and preparing accepted work for the reader.
roles.where: Essay craft from the close-reading unit — a well-structured argument supported by apt quotations — is the standard editors hold manuscripts to; the drama unit's attention to how dialogue works sharpens line edits.

roles.title: News Analysts, Reporters, and Journalists
roles.what: Narrate or write news stories, reviews and commentary for newspapers, magazines, radio and television, collecting and analysing information to inform the public on deadline.
roles.where: Reading unseen texts quickly and writing a structured response — the syllabus's unseen-paper skills — plus the judgement of diction and tone from poetry study, are exactly what daily news writing demands.

roles.title: Technical Writers
roles.what: Write technical materials such as equipment manuals, appendices and operating and maintenance instructions, assisting with layout so complex information reaches users clearly.
roles.where: The close-reading unit's precision with sentence-level meaning — how wording creates effect and where it misleads — is what makes instructions unambiguous; the wider-study unit trains digesting unfamiliar material fast.

roles.title: English Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in English language and literature, including linguistics and comparative literature, at colleges and universities — lecturing, leading seminars and publishing criticism or creative work.
roles.where: The set texts and skills here are the bedrock they teach: from Sonnet 18 to Kumukanda, Pride and Prejudice to When We Were Birds, plus the theory unit from formalism to postcolonialism that frames university-level study.
